questions.question: At 80,000 accepted messages per second, 24 online recipient sessions per message, and 4% retries, how many delivery attempts must fan-out handle each second?
questions.explanation: Fan-out multiplies the source rate by recipients and retry amplification: 80,000 x 24 x 1.04 = 1,996,800 delivery attempts per second.

questions.question: When should the sender receive an accepted acknowledgement?
options: As soon as the gateway reads the socket frame
After every online recipient confirms display
After authorization, channel sequencing, and the durable message/outbox append succeed
After search indexing finishes
questions.explanation: The acknowledgement should prove that the authorized, ordered message is durable and replayable. Recipient delivery and search may complete asynchronously.

questions.question: What ordering guarantee is practical for independent chat channels?
options: One global sequence across every server and direct message
A monotonic sequence within each channel, with gaps replayed before newer messages display
Arrival order at whichever gateway is fastest
No ordering because delivery is real time
questions.explanation: Per-channel sequencing matches the user-visible conversation boundary without coordinating unrelated channels through one global bottleneck.

questions.question: Presence is unavailable, but durable messaging dependencies are healthy. What is the best degraded behavior?
options: Reject all new messages until every status is accurate
Delete expired channel history
Mark all members permanently offline
Continue messaging and show presence or typing as unknown or unavailable
questions.explanation: Presence is an expiring hint, not message or membership authority. Its outage should reduce status fidelity before it reduces durable messaging availability.

questions.question: Fan-out workers are receiving more delivery attempts than their operating capacity. What happens without admission control or more consumers?
options: Queue depth and oldest-message age grow even if sender acknowledgement remains fast
Messages become exactly once automatically
Channel sequence numbers stop being needed
The presence service becomes the history store
questions.explanation: Durable acceptance and recipient delivery are separate. If fan-out arrivals exceed service capacity, backlog and recipient-visible lag grow continuously.

questions.question: A client loses its gateway after sending a message and does not know whether the message was accepted. What should it do?
options: Create a new message ID on every retry
Skip reconnect and wait for search indexing
Reconnect, retry the same message ID, and resume from the last contiguous channel cursor
Ask the presence service to assign a new channel sequence
questions.explanation: A stable message ID makes an uncertain send idempotent, while the channel cursor lets the client replay missing sequences without duplicating visible messages.

questions.question: Why prefer at-least-once fan-out with deduplication over claiming exactly-once display across gateways and clients?
options: It removes the need for durable storage
Retries across crashes and uncertain acknowledgements are unavoidable, so stable identity and idempotent display make the guarantee honest and recoverable
It allows messages to appear out of channel order
It makes backpressure impossible
questions.explanation: A sender can crash after a recipient accepts delivery but before the acknowledgement is recorded. At-least-once attempts plus deduplication handle that uncertainty without a distributed transaction through every client.
